series: Walkthrough for the bank Short etsy-offsite-ads-27-48.json, built Oct 7, 2026 for CMO review
hook: An Offsite Ads sale needs $27.48 to keep the same $8
hook_say: This video shows how to price an Etsy item so you keep the same profit, and the higher price it needs when the sale comes through Offsite Ads.

rows.label: Profit you want per sale
rows.say: You want $8 profit on a candle
rows.why: Start with the profit you want to keep from each sale. The example is a candle, and the goal is $8 of net profit.

rows.label: Materials, labor, packaging
rows.why: Then what the candle costs you to make and pack: $6.10 of materials, $3 of labor and $1.10 of packaging. $10.20 in all.

rows.label: Shipping charged, actual cost
rows.why: Shipping goes in as two numbers: the $5.50 the buyer pays, and the $6.25 the label really costs. The 75 cent gap comes out of your profit.

rows.label: Etsy fees at that price
rows.why: Etsy's fees take a share of item plus shipping: 6.5% transaction, 3% plus 25 cents processing, and the 20 cent listing fee. At the list price the sheet finds next, that is $3.06.

rows.label: List price, no Offsite Ads
rows.why: Because the fees grow with the price, the sheet solves backwards from your profit. List at $22.01 and you keep $8.

rows.label: List price, Offsite Ads sale
rows.why: An Offsite Ads sale adds 15% of item plus shipping for shops under $10,000 in sales over the past year. To keep the same $8 on that sale, the list price is $27.48.

fix.label: Ad sale at $27.48 still keeps
fix.say: Price for it and an ad sale still keeps $8
fix.why: Price for the ad fee and an Offsite Ads sale still leaves the $8 you set. Price for the regular sale only, and the ad fee comes out of your $8.
